The Respondents further submitted that the Petitioner has already recovered tariff during the previous tariff periods and approval of the projected tariff, without corresponding enhancement in service, would impose an undue burden on the beneficiaries and would be contrary to the principles of consumer interest envisaged under Sections 61(d) and 61(i) of the Electricity Act, 2003.

109. In response, the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed strictly in accordance with the provisions of the 2019 Tariff Regulations and 2024 Tariff Regulations for true-up of the tariff and determination of the tariff in respect of the transmission assets. The Petitioner further submitted that all claims are based on audited data, normative parameters and the applicable Tariff Regulations and are subject to prudence check by the Commission, which adequately safeguards consumer interest.

110. We have considered the submissions of the parties.  Regarding the Respondents' pleas that the projected tariff for the transmission assets shows an increasing trend during the 2024-29 tariff period without any cost-benefit analysis; and the Petitioner has already recovered tariff during the previous tariff periods, and that approval of the projected tariff is sought without a corresponding enhancement in service, we are of the view that all the claims have been scrutinized based on the applicable Tariff Regulations and are subject to a prudence check by the Commission. Therefore, we do not find any merit in the submissions of the Respondents, and they are accordingly dismissed.

115. This order disposes of Petition No. 343/TT/2025, in accordance with the above
